rationale: This is essentially the archive's ProfitAccelKnowledgeOverCapexTrend and CapexRDOverGoodwillMix recombined into a triple product of nonnegative ranks (which will be dominated by whichever leg is most dispersed), and the LAG of a 5-year trend is cosmetic given the trend's near-perfect year-to-year persistence.

A defensible diagnosis-driven repair of PhysicalShareShiftNoSalesResponse — replacing the mechanically noisy sales-growth gate with a direct gross-profit-productivity payoff test — though it overlaps heavily with the capex-share-versus-gross-profit spread already embedded in ExternalFinancePhysicalTilt and both legs individually resemble known investment/profitability-change anomalies.

This is close to a sign-flipped mirror of the archive's GoodwillSalesYieldShortfall, and the sign logic is internally shaky since acquisitions mechanically raise goodwill and sales together without raising PP&E, so high scores largely identify recent acquirers — a group the well-documented acquisition/asset-growth anomaly says should underperform, contradicting the positive expected sign.

Because the debt-growth gate is a nonnegative rank multiplier, cross-sectional variation is driven mainly by the gross-margin leg, so the signal risks being a repackaged gross-profitability anomaly, and the remaining structure is a component swap on the already-tested KnowledgeLedPPERefresh and DebtPhysicalExpansionLowMoat.

This is an unconditioned difference of two well-known fundamental-volatility anomalies (profitability/earnings stability and investment volatility) with no genuine interaction, so it is both a likely rediscovery and too trivial to distinguish from existing low-fundamental-volatility factors.

The mechanism — purchased intangibles decaying when the supporting tangible base is not maintained — is a genuinely new angle relative to the archive's goodwill signals, though the "− sales growth" leg reintroduces the GoodwillSalesYieldShortfall structure and stacking three bad-news indicators risks simply reproducing a distressed-firm portfolio.
